title: Regularity of Fourier integrals with a continuous bilinear phase
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and Lebesgue measure. Let $a,b\geq1$ be integers, let $L:\mathbf R^a\times\mathbf R^b\to\mathbf R$ be a continuous real bilinear form, and let $f:\mathbf R^a\to\mathbf C$ be measurable. Fix an integer $r\geq0$ and assume $\int\|\xi\|^j|f(\xi)|\,d\xi<\infty$ for every integer $0\leq j\leq r$. Then the Fourier integral $J_L f(y)=\int e^{-2\pi i L(\xi,y)}f(\xi)\,d\xi$ is a $C^r$ function of $y\in\mathbf R^b$.
